questions.q: The natural frequency of an $L - C$ circuit is $125000cycles / s$. When a dielectric medium of dielectric constant $K$ is introduced between the plates of the capacitor, the frequency decreases by $25kHz$. The value of $K$ is
questions.solution:
$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$

When a dielectric is introduced the capacitance becomes

${C ⁡}^{′} = K ⁡ C ⁡$

$⇒ \dfrac{f{⁡}^{'}}{f} = \sqrt{\dfrac{C ⁡}{C{⁡}^{'}}}$

$\dfrac{125000 - 25000}{125000} = \sqrt{\dfrac{C ⁡}{KC}}$

$\dfrac{100}{125} = \dfrac{1}{K}$

$K = \left(\dfrac{125}{100}\right)2 = 1.56$

For LR circuit,

$tan60 = \dfrac{{X}_{L}}{R} ⇒ {X}_{L} = \sqrt{3} R$

For CR circuit

${I}_{rms} = \dfrac{{V}_{rms}}{R} = \dfrac{\text{200}}{\text{100}} = \text{2 Amp}$

$\text{P} = I^{2} \text{R} = 4 \times \text{100} = \text{400 Watt}$

The average power consumed in an AC circuit is given by

$P = \dfrac{{V}_{0}{I}_{0}}{2}cos ⁡ ϕ$

Where $ϕ$ is phase angle and ${V}_{0}$ and ${I}_{0}$ are the peak values of voltage and current respectively.

Given, ${V}_{0} = 200V, {I}_{0} = 2A, ϕ = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

$P = \dfrac{200 \times 2}{2}cos ⁡ \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$= \dfrac{200 \times 2}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 100W$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In an $LCR$ circuit, the resonant frequency is $600Hz$ and half-power points are at $650Hz$ and $550Hz$. The quality factor is
questions.solution:
In $LCR$ series, resonant frequency,

${f}_{r} = 600Hz$

$∴ {\omega}_{r} = 2\pi \times 600Hz$

Frequencies at half power are given as,

${f}_{1} = 550Hz$ and ${f}_{2} = 650Hz$

${\omega}_{1} = 2\pi \times 550Hz$ and ${\omega}_{2} = 2\pi \times 650Hz$

Quality factor, $Q = \dfrac{{\omega}_{r}}{{\omega}_{2} - {\omega}_{1}}$

$= \dfrac{2\pi \times 600}{2\pi \times 650 - 2\pi \times 550}$

$= \dfrac{2\pi \times 600}{2\pi \times 100} = 6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An $AC$ circuit drawing power from a source of angular frequency $50rads^{- 1}$ has a power factor of $\text{0.6}$. In this condition, a resistance of $100Ω$& is present and the current is lagging behind the voltage. If a capacitor is connected in series, then the required capacitance that will result in a power factor of unity is
questions.solution:
As the current lags the voltage, the circuit must contain a combination of resistance and inductance.

Power factor $cos ⁡ ϕ = 0.6$

$⇒ \dfrac{R}{R^{2} + {X}_L^{2}} = \text{0.6}$

$⇒ R^{2} + {X}_L^{2} = \left(\dfrac{R}{0.6}\right)^{2}$

$⇒ {X}_L^{2} = \dfrac{R2}{\left(\text{0.6}\right)^{2}} - R^{2}$

$⇒ {X}_L^{2} = \dfrac{R^{2} \times \text{0.64}}{0.36}$

$∴ {X}_{L} = \dfrac{0.8 R}{0.6} = \dfrac{4R}{3}$

Now we want the power factor $cos ⁡ ϕ = 1$

This is the condition of resonance in which

${X}_{L} = {X}_{C}$

$∴ {X}_{C} = \dfrac{4R}{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{ωC} = \dfrac{4R}{3}$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{3}{4 \times 50 \times 100} = 150\mu F$

questions.q: In a series $LCR$ circuit, the voltage drop across the resistance is $8V$, across the inductor is $6V$ and across the capacitor is $12V$. Then,
options: the voltage of the source will be leading the current in the circuit
the voltage drop across each element will be less than the applied voltage
$the power factor of the circuit will be \dfrac{4}{3}$
questions.solution:
Since, $cos ⁡ ϕ = \dfrac{R}{Z} = \dfrac{IR}{IZ} = \dfrac{8}{10} = \dfrac{4}{5}$

(Also $cos ⁡ ϕ$ can never be greater than $1$)

Hence, (c) is wrong

Also $I{X}_{C} > I{X}_{L} ⇒ {X}_{C} > {X}_{L}$

$∴$ Current will be leading.

In an $LCR$ circuit,

$V = \sqrt{{\left({V}_{L} - {V}_{C}\right)}^{2} + {V}_R^{2}} = \sqrt{{\left(6 - 12\right)}^{2} + {8}^{2}}$

$V = 10V$, which is less than the voltage drop across the capacitor.

questions.q: A transformer is used to light a $100W$ and $110V$ lamp from a $220V$ mains. If the current is $0. 5A$, the efficiency of the transformer is<!-- MathType@End@5@5@ -->
questions.solution:
Given: Output power, $P = 100W$

The voltage across the primary coil, ${V}_{p} = 220V$

Current in the primary coil, ${I}_{p} = 0. 5A$

The efficiency of a transformer, $\text{η} = \dfrac{\text{output power}}{\text{input power}} \times 1 0 0$

$= \dfrac{P}{{V}_{p}{I}_{p}} \times 100 = \dfrac{100}{220 \times 0.5} \times 100 \approx 91\text{%}$

questions.q: In the circuit shown in diagram, switch $S$ is closed at time $t = 0$. The charge which passes through the battery in one time constant is
questions.solution:
The current at time t is given by

        $i = {i}_{0}\left(1 - {\text{e}}^{- t / τ}\right)$

Here,${i}_{0} = \dfrac{E}{R}$ and $τ = \dfrac{\text{L}}{\text{R}}$

$∴ \text{q} = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{τ}\text{i}\text{d}\text{t} = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{τ}{\text{i}}_{0}\left(1 - {\text{e}}^{- \text{t} / τ}\right)\text{d}\text{t}$

         $= \dfrac{{\text{i}}_{0}τ}{\text{e}} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\text{E}}{\text{R}}\right)\left(\dfrac{\text{L}}{\text{R}}\right)}{\text{e}}$

         $= \dfrac{\text{EL}}{{\text{eR}}^{2}}$

For the bulb to be operated at its rated value the rms current through it should be $1A$

$∴ 1 = \dfrac{200}{{100}^{2} + {( 2\pi50L )}^{2}} ⇒ L = \dfrac{3}{π}H$

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance $10\muF$ is connected to an AC ammeter. If the source voltage varies as $V = 50\sqrt{2}sin ⁡ 100t,$ the reading of the ammeter is
questions.solution:
$C = 10\muF = 10 \times 1{0}^{- 6}F$

$V = 50\sqrt{2}sin ⁡ 100t$

Reading of ammeter $I = \dfrac{{V}_{rms}}{{X}_{C}}$

${X}_{C} =$ impendence of capacitor

${X}_{C} = \dfrac{1}{\omegaC}$

$I = \dfrac{{V}_{rms}}{\dfrac{1}{\omegaC}}$

${V}_{rms} = \dfrac{V}{2} = \dfrac{50\sqrt{2}}{2} = 50V$

Reading of ammeter $I$

$= 50 \times 100 \times 10 \times 1{0}^{- 6}A$

$= 50 \times {10}^{- 3}A ⇒ 50mA$

questions.q: An inductor of inductance $2.0\text{mH}$ is connected across a charged capacitor of capacitance $5.0\mu\text{F}$ and the resulting L-C circuit is set oscillating at its natural frequency. Let $\text{Q}$ denote the instantaneous charge on the capacitor and $\text{I}$ the current in the circuit. It is found that the maximum value of $\text{Q}$ is $\text{200}\mu\text{C}\text{.}$ When $\text{Q} = \text{100}\mu\text{C,}$ what is the value of $\left|\text{dI} / \text{dt}\right|$?
questions.solution:
This is a problem of L - C oscillations.
Charge stored in the capacitor oscillates simple harmonically as

$\text{Q} = {Q}_{0} sin( \omega\text{t} \pm ϕ )$

Here, ${Q}_{0} =$ maximum value of $\text{Q} = 200\mu\text{C} = 2 \times {10}^{- 4} \text{C}$

$\omega = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\text{LC}}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\left(2 \times {10}^{- 3}\right) \left(\text{5.0} \times 1 {0}^{- 6}\right)}} = {10}^{4}{& s}^{-1}$

At $\text{t} = 0, \text{Q} = {Q}_{0}$ then

$\text{Q}( \text{t} ) = {Q}_{0} cos\omega\text{t}$ ... (i)

$\text{I} \left(\text{t}\right) = \dfrac{\text{dQ}}{\text{dt}} = - {Q}_{0} \omega \text{sin} \omega \text{t} & $ and ... (ii)

$\dfrac{\text{dI} \left(\text{t}\right)}{\text{dt}} = - {Q}_{0} {ω}^{2} \text{cos} \left(\omega \text{t}\right) & & & & & & & & & & & & $ ... (iii)

$\text{Q} = 100\mu\text{C}$ or $\dfrac{{Q}_{0}}{2}$

$\text{cos} \omega \text{t} = \dfrac{1}{2}$ or $\omega \text{t} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$\left|\dfrac{\text{dI}}{\text{dt}}\right| = \left(\text{2.0} \times 1 {0}^{- 4} \text{C}\right) { \left(1 {0}^{4} s^{-1}\right)}^{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)

\left|\dfrac{\text{dI}}{\text{dt}}\right| =1 0000 \text{A}$/ $\text{s}$
